claim: For 0<omega<1, 1<q<2 and the real Lorentz sequence plane d^(2)(omega,q) with norm (max(|x1|,|x2|)^q+omega min(|x1|,|x2|)^q)^(1/q), put rho=omega^(1/(2-q)). The exact Ptolemy constant of its dual is (1+rho^2)^((2-q)/q) max{1,2/(1+omega)^(2/q)}. By the previously known primal and endpoint calculations, the primal and dual constants agree for every 0<omega<1, 1<=q<infinity.

correctness.rationale: The dual support-function optimization over x1>=x2>=0 gives N*(M,m)=(M^p+omega^(1-p)m^p)^(1/p) for m<=omega M and (M+m)/(1+omega)^(1/q) otherwise (p=q/(q-1)). The ratio to Euclidean norm has unique first-branch minimum at rho=omega^(1/(2-q)), and maximum at the axis or diagonal. Euclidean Ptolemy yields (b/a)^2, attained by explicitly constructed triples in both weight regimes. Parameter endpoints and the phase boundary are treated as stated.

scientific_limitations: The new computation is real, two-dimensional and 1<q<2. The all-exponent equality uses already established boundary and q>=2 cases. No claim for dimension>2 or complex spaces.

value.rationale: The exact formula completes the dual side of an explicit natural open parameter range from the primary literature, determines the weight phase boundary and produces sharp attaining triples; it yields the full primal-dual equality for this two-dimensional Lorentz family. It does not assert a general duality theorem for arbitrary Banach spaces.
